question: Can the pinned Isaac Sim 6.0.1 headless environment trigger any GenericModelOutput Writer callback for its own built-in Example_Rotary lidar and official simple-cube scene?
why: The exact custom USDA passes creation, SensorChecker and attribute identity. V2 then matched the bundled standalone Writer pattern but received zero callbacks and timed out draining pending writer schedules. A built-in official control is the minimal A/B needed to distinguish host/headless Replicator scheduling failure from custom sensor/scene coupling.
method: Reproduce only the official inspect_lidar_gmo Writer plumbing with Example_Rotary and the official simple cube arrangement in the same pinned headless image. Record callback count, valid-GMO count, zero-element count and writer-drain status. Do not save samples for learning and do not substitute the built-in sensor into the project pipeline.
decision_rule: If callbacks remain zero, classify the blocker as host/headless Replicator runtime scheduling and stop custom-profile work. If callbacks occur with legal GMO, classify the blocker as custom USDA or custom scene/render-product coupling and submit a separate one-factor audit; do not silently apply a fix.
stop_rule: One run only. No Cano, custom sensor, fallback into project data, training, image/driver changes, async/orchestrator patch, retry, or 24-pose restoration. No visualization is required because the research question is callback health; machine callback/GMO metrics and logs are the evidence.

approval.confirmation_reference: User message after reviewing this proposal: 继续

execution_result.root_cause: config=Example_Rotary resolved to the remote Isaac 6.0 asset root while the approved container had --network none; sensor creation failed before Writer attachment or frame updates.
execution_result.scientific_conclusion: The run does not classify headless Writer runtime health and does not distinguish runtime scheduling from custom sensor/scene coupling.
